role: Senior Finance Data Analysis Engineer (BI Developer / Consultant)

evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Identify and troubleshoot data quality issues and discrepancies, ensuring accurate, timely, and reliable data availability.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities emphasize data quality, UAT, report change control, and governance with no velocity/speed language present, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Design and implement data models and schemas tailored for financial reporting, analysis, and decision-making.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: The role directly supports financial reporting and decision-making for Lenovo's Finance team, a financial-reporting context, though it's internal BI/reporting rather than external regulatory disclosure, placing this at moderate rather than high.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role supports an established Finance function at a large, publicly listed global company ($83B revenue) with existing ERP/GL/CRM source systems and centralized data platforms already in place, indicating a mature, specialized organization.
evidence.jd_authorship: Develop, maintain, and optimize ETL pipelines to integrate data from source systems (e.g. ERP, GL, CRM) into centralized data platforms.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name specific tools and systems (Power BI, DAX, RLS, ERP/GL/CRM, Talend/Informatica/SSIS) that show what the role does day to day, though phrasing stays fairly standard BI-consultant boilerplate.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Act as a BI Developer / Consultant, supporting Lenovo's Finance team in digital transformation and analytics initiatives.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role explicitly supports Lenovo's Finance team with financial reporting, FP&A, and finance-domain data models, a finance orientation.
evidence.autonomy_level: Drive project execution by tracking progress, providing regular updates, and working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure timely delivery.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: All responsibilities are scoped execution verbs (act as, collaborate, design and implement, develop/maintain/optimize, drive project execution, identify and troubleshoot, support, manage) responding to defined business needs rather than setting new strategic direction.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: Lenovo's company description mentions AI-enabled products, but no AI skill or tooling is expected of the candidate in their own analytics work.
evidence.testing_framing: Support User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for dashboards and reports, including user training, Q&A, and issue resolution.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: UAT and data quality troubleshooting are framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership language (support, identify and troubleshoot), not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Identify and troubleshoot data quality issues and discrepancies, ensuring accurate, timely, and reliable data availability.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data quality, accuracy, and reliability are named as ongoing secondary concerns without regulatory or stakeholder-trust framing dominating the JD, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Continuously support structural and business changes, including data integration, standardization, and governance initiatives.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Responsibilities are dominated by maintain/support/optimize verbs applied to existing centralized data platforms and BI solutions rather than building new infrastructure from scratch, indicating fix/scale.
evidence.loss_aversion: Identify and troubleshoot data quality issues and discrepancies, ensuring accurate, timely, and reliable data availability — a secondary operational-quality concern, not a dominant compliance risk register.
